evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Australia's Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world, spread over 344,400 km2.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Logical structure, executive summary, headings, labeled figures. Some formatting errors, Wikipedia used despite ban, bibliography messy but mostly cited.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite
STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Uses Wikipedia 'Timeline of spaceflight' as primary source for launch trade despite instruction Wikipedia not proper source.
Sun-sync inclination vs altitude plot presented without hand calculation of formula i = cos^-1(-2*a^3.5 * RAANdot / (3*J2*R^2*sqrt(mu))) ; value 97.7924 deg stated but derivation missing.
RAAN described as location of launch facility (27.33 deg) - incorrect; RAAN is orbit orientation, not launch longitude.
No orbital maneuver delta-V analysis; claims direct injection but no transfer or maintenance budget.

overall: Solid simple Australian-benefit mission with good STK evidence and end-to-end design; minor technical gaps and referencing issues but meets all Part 2 deliverables.

feedback.summary: You delivered a solid, end-to-end Australian-benefit mission for Great Barrier Reef monitoring that meets all Part 2 deliverables. Your STK evidence, COE table p12, and segment coverage are strong. To lift further, fix the 4 technical gaps on p7, p11, p13, p17 and tighten referencing/formatting.

criteria.C1: You did well framing a clear Australian benefit on p4-5, defining fluid-lensing coral monitoring and justifying a single satellite for CSIRO/BOM users with references. For Accomplished 9-10, deepen literature comparison to existing ocean-color missions and quantify the gap yours fills.
criteria.C2: You covered all segments well: Vega E piggyback from Kourou p9, SSO 600km 97.79deg with COEs p12, STK access p14, and drag-sail EOL. To reach 9-10, add the hand-calculation for p11 SSO inclination, correct RAAN definition p13, and include a delta-V budget for p17 maneuvers/maintenance.
criteria.C3: You summarized launch, orbit, ground station and science goal clearly on p18 and linked back to bleaching. Accomplished is strong; for top of band add specific performance numbers from your design e.g., revisit, coverage % and residual risks.
criteria.C4: You provided a logical structure, executive summary p2, and labelled STK figures p10. To reach higher Accomplished, remove Wikipedia as primary source p7 per instructions, fix bibliography consistency, and proof figures/tables formatting.

next_steps: On p11, show full hand derivation i = cos^-1(-2*a^3.5*RAANdot/(3*J2*Re^2*sqrt(mu))) and compare to STK 97.7924 deg for SSO validation.
Correct p13 RAAN concept and on p17 add a simple delta-V budget: direct injection vs maintenance and deorbit, even if zero, with justification.
Replace p7 Wikipedia Timeline with launch provider manual or SpaceflightNow/industry source and standardize references to ensure in-text citations match list.
